detail: All baselines 256 done. AdaIN: CLIP-S=0.5547, LPIPS=0.7142. WCT: CLIP-S=0.5599, LPIPS=0.7177. SAMST: CLIP-S=0.5584, LPIPS=0.5824. SaMam: CLIP-S=0.5837, LPIPS=0.3584. Inference: AdaIN 35s, WCT 65s, SAMST 32s. Eval: 22s each.

Creating 256 vs 512 comparison document. Key finding: at 256, all baselines converge to CLIP-S~0.55-0.58. SaMam is most robust (512->256 delta only +0.002). AdaIN/WCT/SAMST lose significant style transfer capability (delta -0.06 to -0.15). Our model (latent256 e10 CLIP-S=0.7168) dominates all baselines at 256.

512 AdaIN/WCT/SAMST values from unified_results.json computed via src/utils/run_evaluation.py (possibly single style ref). 256 values computed via eval_samam_metrics_phase2.py (all style images avg). SaMam 512 uses same eval_samam_metrics_phase2.py so directly comparable. Cross-method 256 vs 512 ranking may be affected by eval methodology.

Created docs/baseline_256/compare_256_vs_512.md. Key findings: (1) Our model dominates all baselines at both 256 and 512, margin widens at 256 (+0.133 vs +0.021 at 512). (2) Baseline ranking changes: 512 WCT>AdaIN>SAMST>SaMam, 256 SaMam>WCT>SAMST>AdaIN. (3) SaMam most resolution-robust (ΔCLIP-S=+0.002), WCT most sensitive (Δ=-0.146). (4) Main conclusion (our model dominates) is consistent across resolutions.

SAMST/SaMam latent migration both assessed as HIGH difficulty and SKIPPED per user instruction (迁移难度大就算了). SAMST: TransformerNet arch is pixel-specific (3-ch input, 2x down/up sampling), migration requires fundamental redesign. SaMam: mamba SSM advantage disappears on short latent sequences (4x16x16=64-256 tokens vs 256x256=1024+ tokens), requires full retraining. Documented in compare_256_vs_512.md section 6.
